output: A study looked at two ways to use steroids to help people with a condition called primary sclerosing cholangitis. But the studies weren't perfect because some people left the studies before they finished, which might have affected the results. The evidence isn't very strong because the studies are quite old and newer treatments like anti-VEGFs are now used more often. The researchers think laser treatment is still helpful, especially for people with a more serious form of diabetic retinopathy. They want to do more studies to see if combining laser treatment with newer treatments would work even better.

This study looked at 66 articles published between 1988 and 2012 that talked about using a special kind of imaging called Endoscopic Ultrasound (EUS) to find out more about a type of cancer called gastric cancer. They studied 7747 patients who had their cancer checked with EUS. Most of these studies did a good job, but some had small problems that might have affected the results a little bit.

The study found that EUS is very good at telling if the cancer has spread deep into the stomach wall (T3-T4) compared to just being on the surface (T1-T2). It's also pretty good at telling if the cancer is early (T1) or has started to go deeper (T2).

However, when trying to tell if the cancer is just on the surface (T1a) or has gone a little deeper (T1b), or if there are cancer cells in the lymph nodes (N-stage), EUS isn't as good. The results varied a lot between different studies, which means we need more information to understand why.

Overall, while EUS helps doctors understand where the cancer is, it's not perfect. Doctors should be careful when using it and look for other ways to confirm or rule out the cancer. More research is needed to figure out why the results vary so much.
